topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: To mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band, adaptive beamforming techniques can be employed to dynamically adjust transmit and receive beams in response to frequency-dependent steering errors caused by beam squint. This involves optimizing the array factor's phase derivative to minimize beam squint-induced capacity losses. Additionally, considering the increased path loss and limited ray spreading in higher frequency bands, narrower beams may be used to compensate for large path loss, but this limits the effective spread of rays, altering selectivity properties. Furthermore, machine learning-based optimization can be used to predict optimal array factor configurations for various frequency bands and interference scenarios.
